etymologies.etymologyHTML: Formed in Modern English as capable +‎ -ity.

definitions.definition: the power or ability to generate an outcome
(computing) A digital token allowing a user or process to interact in a specified way with an object that is subject to access control. [from 1960s]

quote.citation: 1987 November, Richard Y. Kain, Carl E. Landwehr, “On Access Checking in Capability-Based Systems”, in IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering‎[1], volume SE-13, number 2, pages 202–207:
quote.text: Enforcing a security policy means controlling the rights users can acquire to data. In a capability machine, a user’s rights are defined by the capabilities he (or a process acting on his behalf) can obtain and the access rights conferred by those capabilities.
